title: Data preparation and train/test splits
summary: Split a dataset into training and test sets correctly, and explain why testing on unseen data matters.
objectives: Separate a DataFrame into features X and a label y
Split X and y 80/20 with train_test_split and a fixed random_state
Read the shape of each split to confirm the 80/20 proportion
Explain why the test set must never be used during training

segments.title: What you will build
segments.body:
## What you will build

A model that is tested on the same rows it learned from can look perfect while knowing nothing, like a student who only practises the exact questions that will be on the exam. The fix is to hold back part of the data as a **test set** that the model never sees during training. In this lab you will load `students.csv` (40 fictional students: hours studied, attendance, sleep hours and whether they passed), separate the features `X` from the label `y`, and split them 80/20 with `train_test_split` using `random_state=0` so the split is the same every run. You will print the shape of each of the four pieces to confirm that 32 rows went to training and 8 to testing, and write one sentence explaining why the test rows must stay unseen until the very end.

lab.title: Split the student data 80/20
lab.objective: Separate features from the label, split them 80/20 with a fixed random_state, print the four shapes and explain why the test set stays unseen.
lab.instructions:
The file students.csv has 40 rows and four columns: hours_studied, attendance, sleep_hours and passed (1 = passed, 0 = failed). The starter code already loads it into df.

1. Make X = df[["hours_studied", "attendance", "sleep_hours"]] (the features) and y = df["passed"] (the label).
2. Split them with X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=0).
3. Print the four shapes, one per line, exactly like this:
X_train: (32, 3)
X_test: (8, 3)
y_train: (32,)
y_test: (8,)
4. Store one sentence (at least 8 words) in why_split that explains why the test set must never be used during training. Mention the test set and say that it must stay unseen (new to the model), so its score is honest.

print("X_train:", X_train.shape) prints a shape in the right form; .shape gives (rows, columns) for a DataFrame and (rows,) for a Series.
lab.constraints: Use train_test_split from sklearn.model_selection with test_size=0.2 and random_state=0. Keep the names df, X, y, X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test and why_split. Do not change students.csv. No input().

hints: Columns come out of a DataFrame with square brackets: a list of names gives a DataFrame, X = df[["hours_studied", "attendance", "sleep_hours"]], and one name gives a Series, y = df["passed"].

train_test_split returns four things in this order: X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=0). test_size=0.2 keeps 20% (8 of the 40 rows) for testing and random_state=0 makes the shuffle the same every run.

Print each shape with its name, for example print("X_train:", X_train.shape). Then write the sentence, for example why_split = "The test set must stay unseen during training so its score is an honest check on new data."

lab.solution:
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

df = pd.read_csv("students.csv")

X = df[["hours_studied", "attendance", "sleep_hours"]]
y = df["passed"]

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=0)

print("X_train:", X_train.shape)
print("X_test:", X_test.shape)
print("y_train:", y_train.shape)
print("y_test:", y_test.shape)

why_split = "The test set must stay unseen during training so that its score is an honest check of how the model does on new data."
